newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND SEEK REPEAT OF WORLD CUP SEVENS SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND SEEK REPEAT OF WORLD CUP SEVENS SUCCESS.

text.p: England, surprise winners of the first World Cup Sevens in 1993 with a team of virtual unknowns, will rely on several of their Five Nations championship stalwarts to retain the Melrose Cup when the 24-team tournament starts on Friday.

England internationals Tim Rodber, Richard Hill, Mike Catt, Jon Sleightholme, Austin Healey and Neil Back are joined by four survivors from the side which beat Australia to lift the trophy at Murrayfield four years ago and there is a confident air about the team.
Rodber, who was also in the 1993 squad, has replaced the sidelined Lawrence Dallaglio as captain but that has been the only hiccup in England's preparations.

"Dallaglio's loss is a blow but Richard Hill is a great replacement," said England coach Les Cusworth. "As usual at sevens, New Zealand and Fiji will be hard to beat but I would like to think we are capable of winning.
"We are here to launch a serious defence of our title. It is time to stand up and be counted."

England take on Zimbabwe and Canada on the opening day but those matches are largely irrelevant as the teams will be seeded from one to 24 after the opening group matches and re-drawn into eight groups of three for the second day when the real action will begin.

New Zealand have won the last three Hong Kong Sevens, regarded as an unofficial world championship, but are missing key players in Jonah Lomu and Christian Cullen, through sickness and injury, and the ineligible duo of Waisake Masirewa and Joeli Vidiri.
All four were in the side which won last years's Hong Kong Sevens with Cullen scoring a record 18 tries and succeeding Lomu as "Player of the Tournament" after several electrifying displays.
New Zealand captain Eric Rush still has plenty of sevens experience to call on in the shape of Glen Osborne, Dallas Seymour and Joe Tauiwi but admitted that they will miss the Lomu factor.

"Jonah (Lomu) really wanted to play the World Cup Sevens but he has got to start thinking about himself and his health first. Although we would love to have him in the side we have just got to do the job without him now," said Rush.
"We have a couple of young guys here, nothing like Jonah just yet, but they are ready to shine."

Fiji, seven-time winners of the Hong Kong Sevens and breathtakingly brilliant at the abbreviated game, have been eclipsed by the awesome All Blacks in recent years and are looking to playmaker Waisale Serevi and fast men Manasa Bari and Jope Tuikabe to rekindle their fortunes.
"A lot of our players are based overseas and we could have done with more time to prepare the side," said manager Jone Buakula.

Wales had hoped to mount a serious challenge for the Melrose Cup but their side has been decimated by injury and late withdrawals. Jonathan Davies, Rob Howley, Neil Jenkins and Scott Gibbs were all hurt during last Saturday's Five Nations clash with England while winger Ieuan Evans has opted to stay at home because his wife is expecting a baby.

Super 12 commitments have hit the Australian squad hard but winger David Campese, the world's leading international try scorer with 64, asked New South Wales to release him so he could play in Hong Kong, one of his favourite rugby arenas.
Campese retired from international rugby last year after gaining 101 caps but has opted for another tilt at glory.

The Cook Islands, where just about every male in the 18,000 population plays rugby, Morocco, Portugal and Zimbabwe are the newcomers to the World Cup which will be played before a capacity 40,000 crowd at the Hong Kong Stadium on Friday, Saturday and Sunday.
